title: x1.25/x1.50: QoS manual-editor weight values render inside the scaled minus buttons (labels, split bar, queue-depth row left at x1.00 geometry)
detail: r2 scaled the nudge rects (B5 fix) but left the lane labels, weight values, split bar and queue-depth row at raw x1.00 positions/fonts. At x1.50 lane 0's minus button spans x60-90 while the weight text draws at raw x64 — the digits render inside the button. R1 was internally consistent here; r2 introduced the divergence.
recommended_fix: Route the editor's label x, weight x, bar x/width and queue-depth offsets/fonts through hud()/hud_f() to match the scaled rects.

title: still present since round 1: SLA gauge text scales but row pitch (16px) and hit rect (740x18) do not — overlapping rows at x1.25+
detail: hud(16) gives 20px text at x1.25 and 24px at x1.50 on a raw 16px pitch — rows overlap by 4px/8px, and the raw 740x18 focus hit rect no longer matches the drawn text. Identical to the r1 warning; r2 touched the gauge draw line but not the pitch/rect.
recommended_fix: Scale the row pitch and sla_row_rect height/width through hud() so pitch, text and hit rect stay in step.

title: still present since round 1: draw_hud scales fonts but not y anchors — x1.50 title (33px at y=10) overlaps the hint row (y=36)
detail: At x1.50 hud(22)=33px title at y=10 occupies y10-43; the hint row stays at raw y=36 — 7px of glyph overlap. Same pattern at y=56/68/76/104 (score, toast, lead line, retry). Identical to the r1 warning; r2 scaled the fonts on these exact lines and left the anchors raw.
recommended_fix: Scale the y anchors through hud() or derive each row from the previous row's scaled height.

title: Panel footer 'S / tap chip to close' is false when the panel is open with a pipe selected — S is collected only when sel_pipe < 0
detail: Select a pipe, then open the panel via the chip tap or pad Y: panel_open with sel_pipe >= 0. Keyboard S is then never collected (and phase-2 is panel-blocked), so S does nothing — only Esc/chip close. The footer over-promises for that state.
recommended_fix: Collect S unconditionally while panel_open (the executor's Set_Lane is sel_pipe-gated and phase-2 is suppressed anyway), or make the footer read 'Esc / tap chip to close'.

title: still present since round 1: the new modal left-press comment contradicts the placing gate — placement armed + panel open leaves mouse row taps dead
detail: Arm placement (router chip), then open the panel (chip tap or pad Y): placing_eff >= 0 skips on_ui_press, and the panel_open branch suppresses everything else — panel rows/chip are unclickable by mouse until Esc. The r1 note's case is unchanged; the new 7.3 comment now asserts the opposite.
recommended_fix: While panel_open, run on_ui_press regardless of placing_eff (or fix the comment to state the placing gate).

title: Phase-1 key buffer ([10]Key) is one short of the 11 collectible keys — a same-frame full chord silently drops the last key (M)
evidence:
keys: [10]Key
	keys_n := 0
...collectible cases:
		case .P, .Space:
		case .D:
		case .T:
		case .M:
		case .S:
		case .Up, .Down, .Left, .Right, .Enter:
		case .Esc:
each guarded by `if keys_n < len(keys)` — P/Space share one slot, so 11 distinct keys are collectible into 10 slots.
detail: The diff added 5 collectible keys (S/arrows/Enter) but grew the buffer 5->10; the collectible set is 11. In an 11-key same-frame chord the guard silently drops the 11th (poll order makes it M). Pre-existing pattern (6-in-5), extremely unlikely to fire, but the r1 fix guidance said [11]Key.
recommended_fix: Grow the buffer to [11]Key (or [12]Key for headroom) so the guard can never trip.

title: still present since round 1: unused import "core:strings" in palette.odin
evidence:
import "core:encoding/json"
import "core:strings"
import rl "vendor:raylib"
— grep of app/render/palette.odin for `strings.` returns zero references (the new parse_mode_table copies id bytes with a manual for-loop).
detail: The 7.3 rework added no strings.* usage; the import stays dead. Builds stay green (Odin does not error on it), so this is hygiene only — identical to the r1 note.

title: still present since round 1: PALETTE_MODE_COUNT is dead — cycle_palette re-derives the count inline
detail: The r1 note flagged PALETTE_MODE_COUNT + step_of as dead exports. R2's settings_test now references step_of, but PALETTE_MODE_COUNT still has zero references — the r2 cycle helper duplicates the enum-max arithmetic instead of using it.
recommended_fix: Use PALETTE_MODE_COUNT in cycle_palette (and the settings range check) or drop the constant.
